[ASSISTANT_SAID] The first Leica camera, the Ur-Leica, was created by Oskar Barnack in 1913, and the first commercially available Leica camera, the Leica A, was released in 1925.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Leica A introduced the concept of a compact, portable, and lightweight 35mm camera that used standard cinema film.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Oskar Barnack was inspired to create a camera that would fit in a pocket, allowing photographers to capture moments easily.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The name "Leica" comes from a combination of "Leitz" and "Camera."  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The Leica M3 was released in 1954 and is considered one of the greatest cameras of all time.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The M3 introduced several innovations, including a bayonet lens mount and a combined viewfinder/rangefinder design.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] The M3 is known for its exceptional build quality and durability.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] It's unlikely that the user found a genuine Leica M3 for $20, as it is a highly sought-after camera.

[ASSISTANT_SAID] User should check for distinguishing features such as serial number, lens mount, viewfinder type, shutter speed dial location, and film advance lever position to identify the camera.
